scope: The AP-side transport that carries CI primitives from atcmdsrv to the CP, recovered statically from firmware 3.0.2 Build 241129 Rel.3n. Companion to analysis/ci-primitives.json, which owns the service-group and primitive-id namespace. No message was ever sent.

chain: per-command builder, e.g. atcmdsrv 0x40cac for CI_DEV_PRIM_SET_BAND_MODE_REQ
0x7e2c4  marshaller: sizes, allocates, fills the envelope, logs, hands off
0x7f178 -> 0x139d0 (PLT)  socket write on the msocket fd

entry_signature.args: r0 = CI client object, r1 = numeric primId, r2 = reqHandle, r3 = pointer to the primitive payload (may be NULL for zero-length primitives)
entry_signature.guard: `cmp.w r4, #0x11111111` at 0x7cd34 rejects a poisoned/uninitialised client object and returns 8.

wire_format.total_length: 0x1c + payloadLen; the whole buffer is written to the socket

fields.name: primitive_id
fields.evidence: 0x7e316 `strh r6,[r0,#0x10]` - note the id is 16-bit on the wire, which is why the 0xF000 error range fits

fields.name: pad
fields.evidence: not written; implied by the 16-byte inner header

fields.name: reserved
fields.confidence: UNKNOWN - inside the 16-byte inner header but never written on this path

wire_format.note: The inner header is exactly 16 bytes (0x0c..0x1c), matching `inner_length = 0x10 + payloadLen`. The outer 12 bytes are the msocket envelope.

payload_sizing.rule: If primId - 0xF000 <= 7, the size comes from the global CI_ERR u16 table at 0x0bdc3a. Otherwise a tbb switch on svgId-1 selects the group's own u16 size table, bounds-checks primId, and reads size = table[primId].
payload_sizing.size_table_root: 0x0e1084; per-group pointers at +0x04 CC, +0x08 SS, +0x0c MM, +0x10 PB, +0x14 SIM, +0x18 MSG, +0x1c PS, +0x24 DEV
special_cases: DAT (svgId 8) has no size table; sizes are computed at run time by 0x7ef30 from the payload.
DEV primId 0x47 (CI_DEV_PRIM_ENABLE_HSDPA_REQ) is hardcoded to 9 at 0x7f05e.
PS primId 0x42 is hardcoded to 0x5c at 0x7f062.
payload_sizing.confidence: CONFIRMED - the table value for DEV/51 is 32, matching the `movs r2,#0x20` allocation in the SET_BAND_MODE builder.

request_handle.construction: Built in the AT handler prologue (AT*BAND: atcmdsrv 0x38152-0x38174) from a 12-bit wrapping counter in a static halfword, an 8-bit field at bits 12-19, and 2 bits at 30-31. The counter wraps 0xfff -> 0x0b rather than to 0.
request_handle.mutation_in_builder: 0x40cf8-0x40d08 clears bits 20-29 and 31, then reinserts a 4-bit field at bits 20-23. For SET_BAND_MODE that field is the CI networkMode; for the GET variants it is the literal primId (0x35 / 0x37). The purpose of overloading these bits is UNKNOWN.
request_handle.confidence: SUPPORTED INFERENCE for the field roles; the arithmetic itself is CONFIRMED.

device_nodes.note: These three nodes are NOT interchangeable. Only msocket is on the CI request path.

/dev/msocket.role: CONFIRMED: the CI message transport. The fd used by 0x7d0aa is a global set up by the opener at 0x7f074, whose only device string is /dev/msocket (referenced from the literal pool at 0x7f158).
/dev/msocket.carries: metadata and payload together, in one contiguous write

/dev/acipc.role: Referenced once, from 0x5ee4c, in a component unrelated to the CI send path.
/dev/acipc.assessment: SUPPORTED INFERENCE: ACIPC is the underlying AP/CP doorbell/signalling substrate that msocket is layered on, not a separate message channel used by atcmdsrv. The CP side names ACIPCDHISR/ACIPCRDHISR/acipcTx.

/dev/cpmem.role: Referenced from 0x72928 and 0x7f924, outside the CI send path.
/dev/cpmem.assessment: UNKNOWN whether CI payloads ever transit shared memory. On this path they do not: the payload is copied inline into the msocket write.

dump_function.role: Debug decoder for (svgId, primId, reqHandle, payload, len). It is the structure that reveals the whole namespace: a tbb switch on svgId-1 selecting per-group name tables, preceded by the 0xF000 error-range test.
dump_function.note: Called on the send path at 0x7e330, so its argument order is the authoritative reading of the wire fields.

receive_path.confirmation_routing: reqHandle is echoed by the CP and used AP-side to match a CNF to its REQ. The matching code was not traced in this pass.
receive_path.confidence: UNKNOWN for the AP-side CNF demultiplexer

dev_request_dispatch_table.form: 76 entries of {u32 primId, u32 handler|1}, 8-byte stride, extent 0x06f394fc .. 0x06f3977c
dev_request_dispatch_table.verification: Every id resolves to a CI_DEV_PRIM_*_REQ name; primId 0x33 pairs with 0x068afdf1, independently proven to be the SET_BAND_MODE handler by its 0x34 CNF and 32-byte request validation.

internal_signal_table.form: {u32 handler, u32 signalId} pairs with ids around 0x00090c1b-0x00090c21
internal_signal_table.assessment: A distinct CP-internal signal namespace, not CI primitive ids. CI_DEV_PRIM_GET_BAND_MODE_CNF is built by 0x068b0156, which appears in this table rather than the CI table - consistent with the CNF being emitted asynchronously once lower layers respond.

safety: Recovery only. No CI primitive, AT command, or socket write was executed, and no device was contacted.
